user.title: Connect to a ControlByWeb 400 series module
user.description:
For 400 series modules (X-400, X-401, X-404, X-405/406, X-408, X-410, X-412, X-417, X-418, X-420). Use the Administrator login, or the User login if you enabled a Control Page password; leave the password blank if none is set.

Over plain HTTP the password is sent unencrypted (HTTP Basic), which is fine on a trusted network. HTTPS devices use self-signed certificates, so certificate checking is off unless you tick "Verify HTTPS certificate".

discovery_confirm.title: ControlByWeb module found
discovery_confirm.description: A ControlByWeb module was found at {host}. Enter its login to add it.

model.title: Which model is this?
model.description:
Connected. Found: {summary}.
The model is shown on the device in Home Assistant. The module can't report its own model (and may include I/O linked from other modules), so this is a best guess; please confirm or change it.

error.unsupported_device: The device answered, but not like a 400 series module (no state.json). Other ControlByWeb families, such as older WebRelays, are not supported.

data.use_device_names: Use I/O names from the device (experimental)

data_description.onewire_unit: Only used if the device doesn't report a unit itself.
data_description.use_device_names: Names the entities after the names set on the module (read from customState.json). Matching is by position and is only applied when both files agree; see the diagnostics download if it doesn't take effect.
data_description.writable_registers: Registers are read-only sensors by default. Turn this on to get editable number boxes. On an X-404, registers can hold Modbus device data, so only enable this if you want to write them.
data_description.frequency_unit: X-420 frequency input (for example a wind speed sensor). The module scales it with the slope and offset you set, so Home Assistant needs to know the unit. Only used if the device doesn't report one itself.

pulse.name: Pulse relay
pulse.description: Turns a relay on for a set time, then off. The duration applies to this one pulse only; the pulse time saved on the device is not changed.

start_timer.name: Start timer
start_timer.description: Starts a module timer counting down from the given number of seconds. A duration of 0 stops it. Use it on a Timer sensor.

duration.name: Duration
duration.description: Seconds to count down from (0 stops the timer).
